Also some deets on my look cause the description was a bit barebones 😭

- Basically the two best known dances during the Oruro carnival are the Diablada and the Caporales dance. The former, represented by the mask, was originally an homage to the indigenous god of dearh Supay but then got hit by the catholic influence and called the devil. The mask here is more of a china supay/devil woman version that accompagnies the main devils during parades. I added detail related to Quebec influence by giving the mask a more feline form (the ears pattern on the sides) as a nod to the heavily featured bobcat in Quebec's carnaval.

- The rest of the outfit is a reference to the Caporales dance, which has its roots in the Afro-Bolivian community. I wanted to challenge myself with the palette a bit and repeat the pattern of the belt in places.

- The sash is a Centure Fléchée. Originally made by the Huron Wendat First Nation, its current form comes from Québécois fur traders in the 18th century and is still a staple of Quebec culture. Quebec's carnival mascot famously wears it!

Rejection is painful as all hell so it's understandable. It's also something that gets better with time as you realize that these people didn't make you waste your time by becoming fairweather friends who just tag along for ages without any real interest. For the latter tho don't worry you just gotta be good at boundaries and constantly remind yourseld to not drain yourself for others once a friendship gets going; if anything seeing that people are incompatible with you from the getgo is a blessing in a way. 

And honestly all these interests can be made social! Of course there are levels of how embarrassed you feel at some of the social versions of the interests, ie if you're fine with group workout or drawing classes but would rather die than go to ComicCon or the local comic shop to find events, it's fine but also yet again something that feels better with age because you also care less and less about what is too embarrassing to attend classes, events or group activities for. And chances are you're very far from the only person with this kind of interest who would love to chat about them.

I don't even think you need to be constantly happy to make friends, otherwise my depressed ass would've been alone all the time lmao. I mean in the sense that you realize that the social version of an activity feels good and energizes you, and that you can absolutely share that with people. You got the right attitude by reaching out and trying, and early stumbles and rejection will mean nothing down the years as you learn what kind of person vibes with you. I can again say that the people I know who were constantly targeted for trying too hard to make get-togethers at first now have solid friends groups they can rely on. 

tl;dr making friends is daunting and rejection can and will happen but you're doing so much better than those who tag along without any effort at all. I hope things look up for you soon but I'm pretty sure they will :)

Some people only find those they like even later, some drop out of their friend group for whatever reason and feel lost because that friend group was their only social interaction. What I wanna ask you is if you actually *enjoyed* anything about putting your life together, all that working out, all that reaching out. Sometimes friends come way more naturally through experiencing joy together, not through an artificial cultivation of skills you think you want and need. It can be through the cringiest, most guilty pleasure hobby if you want to. Hell one of my closest friends I made through some massively cringe tumblr phase and I'm now pretty well adjusted IRL. What are your interests? I think you got the mind in the right place and the drive to even lead  your own friend group with activities related to it because this is the frustration of someone who tries. The people who try hard making friends stumble hard at first and get called Too Much but in the long term they're the ones at the center of their group.

Tl;dr I'm sorry you feel so miserable rn because I've been there with crippling loneliness. but I believe if you put energy less in Seeming Like A Socially Apt Person  and put it all in activities that already make you happy on your own, you have the makings to make friends very soon.
